title: Yars' Revenge
subtitle: An insect against a fortress
summary: Yars' Revenge is Howard Scott Warshaw's single-screen shooter, published by Atari for the Atari 2600 in May 1982.
body: Yars' Revenge is Howard Scott Warshaw's single-screen shooter, published by Atari for the Atari 2600 in May 1982. The player controls a winged alien fighting the Qotile, an enemy protected by a wall of energy cells. Shooting the wall or eating its cells opens a route for the powerful Zorlon cannon. The small battlefield concentrates the entire struggle into a few moving pieces: a vulnerable target, a pursuing missile and the insect that must prepare its own opportunity to strike.

The Zorlon cannon appears at the left edge and follows the Yar's vertical position. A successful attack therefore needs alignment followed by a quick escape from the cannon's path: its shot can destroy the player too. The colorful neutral zone offers protection from the destroyer missile, but prevents the Yar from firing. Moving between shelter and attack gives the screen a changing rhythm. Meanwhile, the Qotile can turn into a dangerous spinning swirl, making an apparently safe approach suddenly demand another decision.

Warshaw initially received an assignment to adapt the arcade game Star Castle. His work developed into a different game with its own rules and an elaborate science-fiction backstory, which accompanied the cartridge as a comic. That fiction turns the abstract shield and shifting band of color into traces of a conflict between planets. The screen remains immediately readable as a contest of movement and timing, while the illustrated story gives names and motives to the unusual shapes that Atari's hardware brings to life.
story_headings: A cannon that endangers its owner
From an arcade assignment to a new world
